title: Exactness of associated graded-module sheaves on Proj
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{a\geq0}S_a$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring and let $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj]. Let $M_j=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathbf Z}(M_j)_b$, for $j=0,1,2$, be graded $S$-modules, with $S_a(M_j)_b\subseteq(M_j)_{a+b}$. Suppose $u:M_0\to M_1$ and $v:M_1\to M_2$ are degree-preserving $S$-linear maps and $0\to M_0\xrightarrow{u}M_1\xrightarrow{v}M_2\to0$ is exact as a sequence of $S$-modules. Then the associated module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] and the induced sheaf morphisms [lem-sc-p1-proj-tilde-functorial] form a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules: $0\to\widetilde M_0\xrightarrow{\widetilde u}\widetilde M_1\xrightarrow{\widetilde v}\widetilde M_2\to0$. No generation-in-degree-one, Noetherian, or field hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01M7, label lemma-proj-sheaves, final assertion: the associated sheaf functor on graded modules is exact.

proof.text: Let $B$ consist of all $D_+(f)$ with $f$ homogeneous of positive degree. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion] (0), $B$ is a basis of $X$. By [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (1), the sections of $\widetilde M_j$ on $D_+(f)$ are $(M_j)_{(f)}$, the fractions $m/f^r$ with $m\in(M_j)_{r\deg f}$. By [lem-sc-p1-proj-tilde-functorial], the maps on these sections are $u_{(f)}(m/f^r)=u(m)/f^r$ and $v_{(f)}(m/f^r)=v(m)/f^r$. Thus the chart maps to be tested are precisely the degree-zero localized maps of the given graded maps.

source.place: Tag 01M7, label lemma-proj-sheaves (2),(3) and functoriality; Section 01M3, label section-proj, standard-open basis; Tag 01M4, label lemma-standard-open.

proof.text: Extend the grading of $S$ to $\mathbf Z$ by $S_a=0$ for $a<0$. This is a direct-sum grading of the same ring, and it acts on each $M_j$ with the required degree rule: negative-degree scalars are zero and the nonnegative-degree rule is a hypothesis. Fix a homogeneous $f$ of positive degree. Apply [lem-sc-graded-localization-exact] with $A=S$ and $s=f$ to each of the exact triples $0\to M_0\xrightarrow{u}M_1$, $M_0\xrightarrow{u}M_1\xrightarrow{v}M_2$, and $M_1\xrightarrow{v}M_2\to0$. All maps, including the maps involving zero, preserve degree. The lemma gives exactness of their degree-zero localized triples, with the fraction maps of step 1. The localization of the zero module is zero, since every fraction has zero numerator. Consequently $u_{(f)}$ has zero kernel and hence is injective, $\operatorname{im}u_{(f)}=\ker v_{(f)}$, and $\operatorname{im}v_{(f)}=\ker((M_2)_{(f)}\to0)=(M_2)_{(f)}$, so $v_{(f)}$ is surjective. These are exact sequences of $S_{(f)}$-modules and, on forgetting scalars, of additive abelian groups.

source.place: Tag 00CS, label proposition-localization-exact, and the homogeneous degree-zero restriction supplied by lem-sc-graded-localization-exact; applied to standard-open fractions in Constructions Tag 01M7, label lemma-proj-sheaves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-p1-module-basis-exactness] to the scheme $X$, the basis $B$ of step 1, and the module-sheaf morphisms $\widetilde u,\widetilde v$. Despite its id, this lemma is stated for any scheme and any basis. Step 2 verifies all its hypotheses on every member of $B$: injectivity of the first section map, equality of its image with the kernel of the second, and surjectivity of the second. It follows that $\widetilde v\circ\widetilde u=0$, $\widetilde u$ is monic, $\widetilde v$ is epic, and the resulting short complex is exact. This is the asserted short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.
